tldr: Approximate local privacy preserves finitely many genuine treated outcomes when treatment probability is of order \(n^{-1/2}\). The target maximal global experiment combines Gaussian precision \(H=\lambda J\) with independent treated-label Poisson intensities \(\kappa(1-u),\kappa u\). The pure coefficient \(J\) and binary/ternary optimizer split are credited to the pure Gaussian companion. The contribution is an exact defect-preserving three-row extension and its uniform realization for every sequential private transcript. A legal pair-tag corollary excludes the universal common-mixture shortcut. The all-history comparison and a data-only attaining decision yield exact global ATE risk, with certified finite decisions as supporting computation. Weighted adaptive reconstruction is the central open question.
